fixes.title: One clear promise at the top
fixes.now: The page title and the main headline both read "Stop Grinding. Start Scaling. More Profit. Less Chaos. Finally." Five short sentences compete for attention, and the same line is repeated in the browser tab and in search results.
fixes.preview: One promise in your own words, followed by your subheadline, so a remodeler knows in three seconds what you do and for whom.

fixes.title: Your strongest proof, sourced and up front
fixes.now: "Roundtables members increase their annual revenue by an average of 40% in their first year" is a strong claim with no source next to it, and named member quotes sit further down the page.
fixes.preview: The 40% figure next to the headline with a source line, and a named member quote beside it. A sourced number is what both buyers and AI search tools trust.

fixes.title: A search description that says what you do
fixes.now: Your site's search description, the text that usually appears under your name in Google, reads "Reach your remodeling business goals with Remodelers Advantage." It doesn't mention Roundtables, consulting or training, the things remodelers actually search for.
fixes.preview: One plain sentence about what you offer and who it's for, used as your search description and repeated under the buttons: "Peer Roundtables, consulting and training for remodeling business owners."
